questions.prompt: Which pattern matches the word orange only when it stands alone?
questions.explanation: The \b word boundaries require a transition between word and non word characters, so orangutan does not match.

questions.prompt: In \d{1,3}, what does the quantifier {1,3} control?
options: The whole pattern must be one to three characters long
The previous token, one to three times
At least three matches anywhere in the string
Exactly one match, then exactly three matches
questions.explanation: A quantifier always applies to the token immediately before it, here the single class \d.

questions.prompt: Why must the dot before the top level domain in an email pattern be escaped as \., not written as a plain dot?
questions.answer: Because an unescaped dot is a metacharacter that matches any character, while backslash dot matches only a literal dot.
questions.explanation: Without the escape, a value such as user@domainXcom can satisfy the pattern even though it has no real dot.

questions.prompt: Write JavaScript that tests whether the string 4111111111111111 is a 16 digit Visa card number.
questions.explanation: Visa numbers start with 4, so 4 plus 15 more digits gives exactly 16 digits, and the anchors stop the pattern matching inside a longer string.

questions.prompt: Which piece of a strong password pattern requires at least one digit?
questions.explanation: The lookahead (?=.*\d) scans ahead for a digit without consuming anything; the final class only lists which characters are allowed.

questions.prompt: What does box-sizing: border-box change about an element?
options: Width and height include padding and the border
Margins are added inside the width
Borders are drawn outside the layout
questions.explanation: With the default content-box, width plus padding overflows the container, which is why the class resets every element to border-box.

questions.prompt: Why does the registration form in Week 02 set novalidate on the form element?
options: It disables the browser popup so your custom JavaScript messages can show instead
It lets the form submit without any JavaScript
It removes the required attributes from the inputs
It enables the mobile email keyboard
questions.explanation: Without novalidate, the browser shows its own bubble such as Please include an @, which competes with your inline errors.

questions.prompt: What must match for a label to focus its input when the user clicks it?
questions.answer: The for attribute of the label must equal the id attribute of the input.
questions.explanation: That pairing is also what lets screen readers announce which text belongs to which field.

questions.prompt: Write CSS that gives .form-grid two equal columns with a 24px gap, collapsing to a single column on screens narrower than 640px.
questions.explanation: 1fr 1fr splits the row evenly and the media query is what keeps the form usable on phones.

questions.prompt: Which head element makes a page respond to phone screen sizes?
questions.explanation: Without the viewport tag, mobile browsers render a zoomed out desktop page and users have to pinch to read it.

questions.prompt: In a row flex container, which property distributes free space along the main axis?
questions.explanation: justify-content works on the main axis and align-items on the cross axis; they swap meaning if you change flex-direction to column.

questions.prompt: What must a ::before or ::after rule have to render anything at all?
questions.explanation: content is mandatory, even when it is an empty string, otherwise the pseudo-element is never generated.

questions.prompt: In one sentence each, what do Flexbox and Grid each arrange?
questions.answer: Flexbox arranges items along one axis, one row or one column, while Grid places items across rows and columns at the same time.
questions.explanation: That is why a navbar uses flex and a page skeleton or gallery uses grid.

questions.prompt: Write CSS that centres a .hero box horizontally and vertically.
questions.explanation: The container needs a height, here the full viewport, otherwise centring has no space to work in.

questions.prompt: Which tag holds the primary content of a page and should appear only once?
questions.explanation: <main> tells assistive tech where the primary content starts; the others can appear many times on one page.

questions.prompt: What does typeof null return?
questions.explanation: It is a known quirk from the first version of JavaScript, so check for null with value === null instead.

questions.prompt: Given const person = { name: 'Ada' }; which line runs without error?
questions.explanation: const locks the binding, not the object's contents, so mutating a property is allowed while reassigning throws.

questions.prompt: Why does an arrow function not work as an object method that needs this?
questions.answer: An arrow function has no own this binding, so it inherits this from the surrounding scope instead of taking it from the object that called it.
questions.explanation: That inheritance is exactly what you want inside a callback, and exactly wrong for object methods and constructors.

questions.prompt: Given const scores = [45, 82, 91, 37]; write an expression that returns only the scores of 50 or more, sorted ascending.
questions.explanation: filter selects the matching values and sort rearranges them; the compare function stops the default lexicographic order.

questions.prompt: What does a getter in an ES6 class let you do?
options: Read a computed value like a property, for example rect.area
Make every field of the class private
Run code only once when the class is defined
Force a method to become static
questions.explanation: A getter runs on access without parentheses, which keeps the outside code reading like plain data.

questions.prompt: Which jQuery method reads the current value of an input field?
questions.explanation: Inputs have no text node, so .val() is the method that reads and writes what the user typed.

questions.prompt: What problem does event delegation solve?
questions.answer: It attaches one handler to a parent so events from child elements added after page load still trigger it.
questions.explanation: In jQuery you pass the child selector as the second argument to .on(), as in parent.on('click', '.child', fn).

questions.prompt: Write jQuery that changes every .course-card to say Updated, adds the class is-complete, and sets opacity to 0.5.
questions.explanation: Most methods return the same collection, so the three steps chain; a reading call such as .text() with no argument would end the chain.

questions.prompt: A page builds its content after load and has a Load more reports button. Which tool fits?
options: A regular expression on the raw HTML
A CSS selector run in the stylesheet
questions.explanation: Cheerio only reads the HTML you hand it; Playwright drives a real browser so it can wait, click, and then read the new nodes.

questions.prompt: What should you check before scraping a real website?
options: Only the colour scheme of the page
Its terms of use, its robots.txt, and whether an official API exists
Nothing, because public pages are free to copy
Only the errors in the browser console
questions.explanation: Publicly visible content is not automatically unrestricted, and an official API is usually the more stable source.
